subject: Position Announcement: Visiting Assistant Professor in Behavioral Science, Environmental and Water Resources (Delaware State University)
title: Position Announcement: Visiting Assistant Professor in Behavioral Science, Environmental and Water Resources (Delaware State University)
text:
---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Leah H. Palm-Forster via CWAE <cwae@aaealist.org>
Date: Mon, Aug 24, 2026 at 7:34 AM
Subject: [AAEA CWAE] Position Announcement: Visiting Assistant Professor in Behavioral Science, Environmental and Water Resources (Delaware State University)
To: Leah Palm-Forster <leahhp@udel.edu>

Dear Colleagues,
 
We want to highlight a new opportunity at Delaware State University that may be of interest to your students, postdocs, and colleagues. DSU's College of Agriculture, Science and Technology is hiring a Visiting Assistant Professor in Behavioral Science related to Environmental and Water Resources. This position is funded by the National Science Foundation and is a twelve-month faculty appointment based in Dover, Delaware, with 75 percent of effort devoted to research and 25 percent to teaching, student engagement, and experiential learning.
 
The position centers on human behavioral responses to water resource challenges, with particular attention to saltwater intrusion risk and coastal resilience. The successful candidate will design and conduct field and laboratory experiments, develop and implement surveys on public decision making around water management and climate adaptation, and work with interdisciplinary teams studying the biophysical, social, and economic drivers of saltwater intrusion. The role includes collaboration with the University of Delaware's Center for Experimental and Applied Economics and other partner institutions, access to an experimental economics lab, and opportunities to mentor undergraduate and graduate students, co-author peer-reviewed publications, and contribute to policy-relevant research on climate adaptation.
 
A Ph.D. in behavioral science, applied economics, psychology, sociology, or a closely related field with an emphasis on human decision making and behavior is required, along with demonstrated coursework in research methodology, particularly experimental economics, survey research, or related experimental methods.
 
Here’s a link to the full description on the Delaware State University website: https://www.schooljobs.com/careers/desu/jobs/5434146/visiting-assistant-professor-in-behavioral-science-related-to-environmental-and-w .  We are happy to talk about the position, and you can learn more about the hiring process and Delaware State University by contacting the search chair, Dr. Gulni Ozbay (gozbay@desu.edu).
  
Best regards,
Kent Messer & Leah Palm-Forster

subject: Postdoc opportunity in Vermont
title: Postdoc opportunity in Vermont
text:

Date:
August 25, 2026 at 3:37:27 PM GMT+2

To:
Scarlett Zhang via ENV <env@aaealist.org>

Reply-To:
"Horan, Rick" <horan@msu.edu>

Please see the postdoc opportunity announced below:

 

All:

 

I’m hiring a postdoctoral researcher to join applied, community-engaged research on rural economies, climate shocks, and
 food systems. 

This role blends causal-inference and data-visualization work with interviews and focus groups involving New England businesses, municipal leaders, and consumers. Projects examine how severe weather and extreme heat affect rural labor markets, downtown activity,
 recreation, food businesses, and local infrastructure. Funding comes from an NSF EPSCoR grant + funding from the UVM Food Systems Research Institute.

I’m especially eager to hear from candidates with:

• A PhD completed by January 1, 2027 in economics, applied/agricultural economics, regional science, public policy, or a closely related quantitative social-science field

• Strong econometric and programming skills in R, Python, and/or Stata

• Interest or experience in rural development, climate resilience, and/or food systems

• Comfort with both quantitative research and community-engaged fieldwork

Hybrid and remote arrangements are possible for candidates based in the United States, with required periodic travel to Burlington and field sites across New England. The position requires eligibility to work in the U.S. for the duration of the appointment;
 please review the posting for details.

Apply 👉 https://www.uvmjobs.com/postings/87760

 

Please share with strong candidates and relevant networks. Applications close October 31, 2026...any questions please email
 me!

 

__

Andrew J. Van Leuven

Assistant Professor

Department of Community Development & Applied Economics

University of Vermont

209AA Morrill Hall | Burlington, VT 05405

Subject: Two Economist job openings in OCE

 

Hello all - 

 

We are excited to alert everyone to two GS14/GS15 economist openings within OCE.  Both are DC-based positions.

 

The first economist position will be for an economist whose focus will be on agricultural input markets, within OCE’s Immediate Office (IO).  The second economist position will be for a biofuels/trade economist that will work closely
 with both the IO and OCE’s Office of Energy and Environmental Policy.

 

The announcements are located here: 
https://www.usajobs.gov/GetJob/ViewDetails/886719200 and 
https://www.usajobs.gov/GetJob/ViewDetails/886720100. Please note that there are separate application processes for the GS14 and GS15 grades (i.e., applying for a GS14 opening does not mean you have applied for the GS15 opening and vice versa).  So, if
 you want to be considered at either GS14 or GS15 level then you should apply for both.

 

Applications will be accepted until October 8.  Please help us get the word out on these important openings so we can develop a strong candidate pool. 

 

Thanks!

 

Cindy Nickerson

Deputy Chief Economist

 

Jeff O’Hara

Acting Director, Office of Energy and Environmental Policy
